lead: Special casting processes use a precision mould, either expendable or permanent, to make a casting closer to final size than sand casting. The mould may be a thin resin-bonded shell, a ceramic shell around a wax pattern, a steel die, or a rotating mould. The aim is better surface finish, tighter tolerance, thinner walls, or higher production. These processes cost more in pattern or die, so they suit parts where machining is expensive or the volume is high. You see them in pump impellers, turbine blades, automotive housings and pipes.
prereq: You need: sand casting and moulding sand, patterns and allowances and moulding methods.

sections.h3: Shell moulding: resin sand on a hot pattern

blocks.text: Shell moulding uses a metal pattern heated to about 200-300 °C. The pattern is clamped over a dump box of resin-coated sand. The sand is fine silica grain coated with a thermosetting phenolic resin. When the sand touches the hot pattern, the resin cures and a thin shell forms. The box is inverted, loose sand falls away, and the shell is cured further and stripped. Two shell halves are clamped or glued with backing for pouring. The hot pattern is the key: the mould is not heated; only the thin layer next to the pattern sets.

items: Clean and heat the metal pattern to 200-300 °C.
Clamp the dump box over the pattern and tip in resin-coated sand.
Wait a few seconds for a 5-10 mm shell to cure.
Invert the box so loose sand falls back.
Cure the shell in an oven, then strip it from the pattern.
Clamp or glue two halves and back them with sand or metal shot.

blocks.text: Shell moulds give a smooth surface, close tolerance, thin sections and good repeatability. Pattern and resin costs are high, and part size is limited by pattern and shell handling. Typical parts are small gears, camshafts, valve bodies and housings where machining must be low.

sections.h3: Investment casting: a wax pattern becomes a ceramic shell

blocks.text: Investment casting, or lost-wax casting, makes the pattern from wax or a wax-like polymer. The pattern is injected into a metal die and assembled on a central sprue as a tree. The tree is dipped repeatedly into ceramic slurry and stucco; each coat dries, and the built-up ceramic becomes the shell. The shell is heated so the wax melts and runs out, called dewaxing, then fired in a burnout furnace. Molten metal is poured into the hot ceramic shell. After freezing, the shell is broken away.

items: Inject wax into a metal pattern die and remove the wax pattern.
Attach patterns to a central wax sprue to form a tree.
Dip the tree in ceramic slurry and sprinkle stucco; dry and repeat.
Heat the shell so wax melts out; collect or discard the wax.
Fire the empty shell to burn off residue and strengthen it.
Pour molten metal into the hot shell and let it freeze.
Break the ceramic shell and cut the castings from the tree.

blocks.text: Investment casting gives fine detail, thin walls and little or no machining. It casts complex shapes in steel, stainless steel, nickel and cobalt superalloys, aluminium and copper alloys. Uses include turbine blades, pump impellers, jewellery, dental parts and valve components. Limits are many steps, long cycle, expensive wax and ceramic, and usually small to medium size. The pattern is expendable.

sections.h3: Pressure die casting: metal forced into a metal die

blocks.text: Pressure die casting forces liquid metal into a hardened steel die at high pressure. The die has two halves: one carries the cavity, the other the cover. A shot sleeve and plunger push metal through runners into the cavity. Pressure is held until the casting freezes; then the die opens and ejector pins push out the part. The die is water-cooled, so cycles are short and production is high.

In a hot-chamber machine the gooseneck injection cylinder sits inside the molten metal pot. The plunger pushes metal directly into the die. It suits low-melting metals such as zinc, lead, tin and some magnesium. The cycle is fast. It is not used for aluminium because the hot metal attacks the gooseneck and picks up iron.

In a cold-chamber machine metal is ladled into a separate shot sleeve, and the plunger injects it into the die. It suits aluminium, magnesium, copper and other high-melting alloys. The melting pot is separate from the injection system, so high temperature does not damage a gooseneck.

blocks.where: F is the clamping force in N; p is the metal pressure in MPa, with 1 MPa = 1 N/mm²; A<sub>proj</sub> is the projected area in mm² perpendicular to the die opening.

sections.h3: Centrifugal casting: metal thrown to the mould wall

blocks.text: Centrifugal casting uses a rotating mould. Molten metal is poured and centrifugal force presses it against the mould wall. The three modes differ in what rotates and what shape is cast.

items: True centrifugal: the mould rotates about the axis of a hollow casting. No core is needed. Pipes and cylinder liners are made this way. The outer wall is dense; the inner surface holds lighter impurities and is machined off.

Semi-centrifugal: the mould rotates about a vertical central axis. A central sprue feeds cavities arranged around it. Wheels, pulleys and gear blanks are typical. The casting itself need not be hollow.
Centrifuging: small moulds sit around a central sprue in a rotating assembly. Centrifugal pressure fills each mould. Small precise parts are made this way.

examples.question: A die casting has a projected area of 80 cm². The metal pressure is 150 MPa. Find the clamping force needed in MN.
steps: Convert to mm²: 1 cm² = 100 mm², so A_proj = 80 × 100 = 8000 mm².
Use 1 MPa = 1 N/mm², so p = 150 N/mm².
Clamping force F = p × A_proj = 150 × 8000 = 1,200,000 N.
Convert to MN: 1 MN = 1,000,000 N, so F = 1.2 MN.
examples.answer: The clamping force needed is 1.2 MN.
examples.check:
A_cm2 = 80
A_mm2 = A_cm2 * 100
p = 150
F_N = p * A_mm2
F_MN = F_N / 1000000
print(A_mm2)
print(F_N)
print(F_MN)

traps: The clamping force uses the projected area perpendicular to the die opening, not the total wetted surface area of the casting.
Unit slip: 1 MPa = 1 N/mm² and 1 cm² = 100 mm². Convert area before multiplying by pressure.
In shell moulding the metal pattern is heated, not the whole sand box. Only the resin next to the pattern cures.
The investment pattern is wax and is destroyed; it is not a reusable pattern like a metal pattern in sand casting.
Hot chamber is for low-melting zinc, lead and tin; cold chamber is for aluminium and high-melting alloys.

quiz.a: Fine silica sand coated with a thermosetting phenolic resin; it cures on a hot pattern.

quiz.q: Why is the pattern heated in shell moulding?
quiz.a: Heat cures the resin in the sand layer touching the pattern, so a thin shell forms and loose sand can fall away.

quiz.q: A die casting has projected area 50 cm² and metal pressure 120 MPa. Find the clamping force in MN.
Why is hot-chamber die casting not used for aluminium?
quiz.a: Aluminium is high melting; it attacks the gooseneck and causes iron pickup, so a cold chamber is used.

quiz.q: Give two differences between true centrifugal and semi-centrifugal casting.
quiz.a: True: mould axis is the casting axis, makes hollow cylinders without a core. Semi: vertical central sprue feeds outer cavities, casting need not be hollow.

quiz.q: What is dewaxing in investment casting?
quiz.a: Heating the ceramic shell so the wax pattern melts and leaves the cavity.

quiz.q: A small stainless steel impeller needs fine detail and 500 parts per year. Choose shell, investment or die casting, and justify.
quiz.a: Investment casting: it gives fine detail and thin walls in stainless steel; die casting steel is not practical, and shell moulding cannot match the detail; low volume suits investment.

beyond: Not for the exam. Vacuum-assisted die casting pulls gas out of the die before injection, which lowers porosity in safety-critical aluminium parts. Squeeze casting uses low pressure and high pressure solidification to make dense automotive components. Lost-foam casting uses an expendable polystyrene pattern that vaporises when metal enters. Research looks at semi-solid metal (thixocasting) and high-pressure die casting of thin-walled electronic housings. Search for vacuum die casting, squeeze casting, lost foam and thixocasting.
